case_name: Management Of Monghyr Factory Of Itc Ltd.,Monghyr,Bihar v The Presiding Officer, Labour Court Patna (Bihar)& 3 Ors
petitioner: Management Of Monghyr Factory Of Itc Ltd.,Monghyr,Bihar
respondent: The Presiding Officer, Labour Court Patna (Bihar)& 3
facts: From the Judgment and Order dated 23-7-73 of the Patna High Court in C.W.J.C. No. 31 of 1971.
The State of Bihar is respondent no. 4.
Respondent no. 3 was working as an operator on a packing machine in the appellant's factory at Monghyr on May 21, 1966 when he is said to have committed certain acts of misconduct.
A chargesheet was served on him by the Management on May 24.
At the domestic inquiry held by the Management, he was found guilty and eventually dismissed from service on June 9, 1966.
issues: Whether the reference is invalid as it indicates that it was mechanically made by the Government without application of mind.

Whether the workman was guilty of misconduct within the meaning of cl. (ii) of Standing Order 20 applicable to the appellant and both the Courts below have committed errors of law on the face of the record in taking a contrary view.
Whether it was not expedient, fit or proper to order reinstatement of the concerned workman and in lieu thereof, only compensation ought to have been allowed.
petitioner_arguments: That the reference is invalid as on its very face it indicates that it was mechanically made by the Government without application of mind.

That the workman was guilty of misconduct within the meaning of cl. (ii) of Standing Order 20 applicable to the appellant and both the Courts below have committed errors of law on the face of the record in taking a contrary view.

That in any view of the matter on the facts and in the circumstances of this case it was not expedient, fit or proper to order reinstatement of the concerned workman and in lieu thereof, only compensation ought to have been allowed.
respondent_arguments: The reference is valid as it indicates that the Government has applied its mind to the matter.

The workman was not guilty of misconduct within the meaning of cl. (ii) of Standing Order 20 applicable to the appellant and both the Courts below have correctly decided the issue in taking a contrary view.
It was expedient, fit or proper to order reinstatement of the concerned workman and compensation ought not to have been allowed.
court_reasoning: The High Court is required to record the reasons or the grounds for granting the certificate.
Once the certificate is granted and the appeal is lodged in the Supreme Court, it is open to the appellant to raise all grounds which properly arise in the appeal.

The stage at which the High Court considers the grant of a certificate under Art. 133(1) and the stage at which the Supreme Court bears the appeal are two distinct stages, and different jurisdictions are exercised with respect to each stage.
holding: We reject the preliminary objection raised by Mr. Santokh Singh.
The three submissions made on behalf of the appellant are rejected.
